title: The condensed algebraic closure is a coproduct of regular finite-field modules
statement: Fix a prime ell and a finite intermediate field E of Omega, the algebraic closure of Q_ell. On the coherent site of profinite sets, let Ebar be the ring sheaf U |-> C(U,E), and let Omegabar be the finite-subextension-valued continuous-function ring sheaf: a section on U is a continuous U -> Omega whose image lies in one finite intermediate field. Use the internal module categories and regular modules of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], with the canonical pointwise coefficient inclusion Ebar -> Omegabar. For any chosen coproducts indexed in Type (u+1) in Ebar-modules, there is an index type I in Type (u+1) and an isomorphism from the I-coproduct of regular Ebar to the restriction of regular Omegabar.

source.place: continuousBasisIso (sectionwise basis equations), continuousBasisSheafIso (monoidal sheafification transport), lines 267-367; adapted from finite bases using the actual finite-subextension section model in lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/RingObjects/Condensed/FiniteSubextension.lean.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic E-basis of Omega. For a finite intermediate field F, expand a finite Q_ell-basis of F; the union of the supports of its basis vectors bounds the supports of all elements of F, since each coordinate is Q_ell-linear. The restriction of each coordinate to F is continuous by LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional, applied directly over Q_ell. Thus every finite-field-valued continuous section has uniformly finite support and continuous E-valued coordinates.

source.place: continuousBasisIso (sectionwise basis equations), continuousBasisSheafIso (monoidal sheafification transport), lines 267-367; adapted from finite bases using the actual finite-subextension section model in lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/RingObjects/Condensed/FiniteSubextension.lean.

proof.text: For each basis vector x, multiply an E-valued continuous function by x. Its values lie in the finite compositum E with Q_ell(x), and the resulting function is continuous. The basis equations show that summing these scalar sections is inverse to the coordinate map. The construction is natural under precomposition, and multiplication is E-linear by associativity. Hence the resulting presheaf module cofan is a coproduct: forget the module structure, evaluate on U, and identify it with the standard Finsupp coproduct of abelian groups. Reflection by evaluation and the module forgetful functor proves the universal property.

source.place: continuousBasisIso (sectionwise basis equations), continuousBasisSheafIso (monoidal sheafification transport), lines 267-367; adapted from finite bases using the actual finite-subextension section model in lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/RingObjects/Condensed/FiniteSubextension.lean.

proof.text: The sheafification functor is monoidal and preserves colimits. Its module functor preserves coproducts, as is checked after the conservative module forgetful functor. Map the presheaf coproduct isomorphism through sheafification, and use the canonical isomorphisms from the sheafifications of the two presheaves to their ring sheaves. Restriction along the inverse finite-field ring isomorphism preserves coproducts and transports the regular modules and coefficient inclusion, giving precisely the claimed isomorphism for the chosen coproducts.
